clue.text: Local network installed in loft by the ocean

indicators.note: something installed in a space is fitted inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a loft is the room under the roof
LAN stands for local area network

explanation.surface: Someone wires up a home network in their attic, in a house overlooking the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic is one of the world's great oceans, lying between Europe and the Americas.

blocks.note: a million is M, as in the prefix mega
the brackets put one number inside the other, read as the word in
the outer digits 1000 make a thousand, K as in kilo

explanation.surface: A baffling string of digits presented like a puzzle, with the claim that it is an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The million sits inside the thousand, so the number reads M in K: run together, that is MINK.
explanation.definitionFit: The mink is a small carnivorous mammal prized for its fur, so it is a beast.

clue.text: Move around the Tube, essentially underground in America

indicators.note: around means one word wraps itself about another
the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letters are used

blocks.note: to sway is to move to and fro
the two middle letters of the word tube

explanation.surface: Advice on getting about London's Underground, oddly glossed as being American.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's Underground, and Americans call their underground railway the subway.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a subway is an underground railway, what Londoners call the Tube.

clue.text: I serve differently to conclude Federer's final game

indicators.note: arranged differently means the letters are put in another order
the final of a word is its closing letter

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
the last letter of the tennis player's name

explanation.surface: A tennis player resolves to vary their serve to close out Federer's last game.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis setting makes 'game' look like a game in a set; it is a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Reversi is a board game, also sold as Othello, in which counters are flipped to the capturing colour.

clue.text: Bill's old schoolmaster

blocks.note: first meaning: a bird's bill
second meaning: dated British slang for a schoolmaster or magistrate

explanation.surface: A man called Bill remembers his former teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name; it is a bird's bill, and the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's horny mouth is its beak, and old British school slang used the same word for a teacher.

clue.text: Every other Briton's reasonable and related by blood

indicators.note: every other means taking one letter and skipping the next

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters
reasonable means sensible, logical

explanation.surface: A claim that all Britons are sensible and kin to one another.
explanation.definitionFit: A biological parent or child is one related by birth rather than by adoption or marriage.

clue.text: In Judea, the nativity reveals deity

indicators.note: in points to letters sitting inside the words that follow

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A Christmas sentence: the birth in Judea reveals God incarnate.
explanation.walkthrough: The nativity scene suggests the Christian God; the deity is Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was the Greek goddess of wisdom and war, patron of Athens.

clue.text: Bearing thanks, King George departed to tour Thailand

indicators.note: whatever has departed has gone away, so those letters leave
to tour a place is to travel round it, so the word goes around another

blocks.note: gratitude is thankfulness
GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher
T is Thailand's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: Bearing thanks, the late King George set off on a tour of Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: GR, Georgius Rex, is the royal cipher seen on postboxes; 'departed' suggests the late king, but it tells you to remove him.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing in the sense of carriage or posture is attitude, how one holds oneself.

clue.text: Be no longer in the lead?

blocks.note: ex means former, no longer
first place is 1ST, read as letters

explanation.surface: A wistful question about losing first place.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 in 1ST is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, to have being or reality.

clue.text: Support the other side

blocks.note: first meaning: to support someone, as a verb
second meaning: the reverse side of something

explanation.surface: Urging loyalty to the opposing team.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a cause is to support it, and the back is the reverse face of anything.

clue.text: One day in seven I'll eradicate ragwort, primarily with this?

definitions.text: One day in seven I'll eradicate ragwort, primarily with this?

indicators.note: in means one thing is placed inside another
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters count

blocks.note: seven days make a week
D is the abbreviation for day
taken as written, without the apostrophe
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A gardener vows to spend one day a week clearing ragwort, with a hinted chemical aid.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: what a gardener might use one day a week to wipe out weeds like ragwort, a toxic yellow-flowered plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragwort is a common weed, and a herbicide used to eradicate it is a weedkiller.

clue.text: Determined supporter boring Sylvester Stallone

indicators.note: something boring drills into another thing, ending up inside it

blocks.note: Sly is the actor's well-known nickname
a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: A grim, determined fan finds Stallone's films dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull; it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard and resolute like steel, so firmly determined.

clue.text: Delivers suspect walk-on part? I'd stumble over scenery

indicators.note: to stumble is to trip and fall in a muddle, so the letters are jumbled
turned over, in a down clue, means read from the bottom back up

blocks.note: an extra has a walk-on part in a film
taken as written
a stage set is the scenery

explanation.surface: An actor with a bit part worries they'll trip over the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatrical scene hides the definition: 'suspect' is a noun, the person handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: A state that extradites someone hands over a suspect to another jurisdiction for trial.

clue.text: Gary isn't cast in 1960s' TV series

indicators.note: cast can mean thrown, so the letters are flung into new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor named Gary is left out of the cast of an old TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a TV cast list; it is the anagram signal. Stingray was a Gerry Anderson puppet adventure series.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingray was a British puppet series about a submarine, first broadcast in 1964.

clue.text: Announcement: 50% off diamonds!

indicators.note: fifty per cent off means half of the word is cut away

blocks.note: a notice is a public announcement

explanation.surface: A jeweller's sale announcement: diamonds at half price.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of NOTICE goes, leaving its second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is slang for diamonds, from their cold glittering look.

clue.text: E-lation?

blocks.note: surface reading: elation, a state of great joy
setter's reading: the high from taking E, slang for a popular rave drug

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen splits off E, slang for a club drug, so the word means both great joy and the drug that brings it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means rapturous joy and is also the full name of the drug known as E.

clue.text: Runner is climbing over the summit of Kilimanjaro

indicators.note: the summit is the top, and in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter
in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, backwards
going over something means passing across and around it

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the mountain

explanation.surface: An athlete is climbing Kilimanjaro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; it means a runner on a sledge or a pair of snowshoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long narrow runner that slides over snow, like the runner of a sledge.

clue.text: Drunk pinches copper and metal

indicators.note: to pinch something is to grip it, holding it inside

blocks.note: merry is tipsy
Cu is copper's chemical symbol

explanation.surface: A drunk shoplifts copper and other metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinches' reads as stealing; it means holding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is a metallic element, the only metal liquid at room temperature.

clue.text: Just terrible losing crown

indicators.note: the crown is the top, so in a down clue the first letter is lost

blocks.note: frightful means terrible

explanation.surface: A dethroned monarch laments it is simply terrible to lose the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like an adverb, 'simply'; it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Just means fair and legitimate, as does rightful, as in the rightful owner.

clue.text: Common soldier

blocks.note: first meaning: widespread, not specific
second meaning: a senior army officer

explanation.surface: Looks like a private, a common soldier, but it is the top brass.
explanation.definitionFit: General means widespread or usual, and a general is a high-ranking army officer.

clue.text: A British party is caught after doing a U-turn, sharp

indicators.note: a U-turn sends something back the way it came, so it reads backwards
something caught is trapped inside another thing

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for British
a rave is a dance party
taken as written

explanation.surface: A British political party is caught out making a policy U-turn, and the criticism is sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A British party' looks like a political party; the party is a rave.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive means harsh or sharp in manner, rough like sandpaper.

clue.text: Having no immediate use, king leaves in musical style

indicators.note: whatever leaves goes away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: blue-sky research or thinking has no immediate practical application
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A redundant king departs to the strains of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue-sky means speculative, with no practical payoff yet; take away K to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluesy describes music in the style of the blues, with its bent notes and melancholy feel.

clue.text: Sturgeon's playing a bugle

indicators.note: playing about with letters rearranges them

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Sturgeon is playing a bugle.
explanation.walkthrough: Sturgeon looks like a surname, perhaps Nicola Sturgeon the Scottish politician; it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a large sturgeon of the Caspian and Black Seas, source of prized caviar.

clue.text: Adult abandons fight over oxygen container

indicators.note: whatever abandons a word walks out of it, so that letter goes
lying over something means covering it on both sides, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a battle is a fight
A is the film classification for adult
O is oxygen's chemical symbol

explanation.surface: A grown-up gives up a struggle over an oxygen tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Container' looks like part of an oxygen cylinder; it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle is a vessel for holding liquids, a kind of container.

clue.text: Everton gutted — thumps in dodgy penalty

indicators.note: something gutted has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are not in order

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the club's name
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A football report: Everton, devastated, hit back after a dubious penalty call.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is an English football club; 'penalty' suggests a spot kick but means a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A penalty is a punishment imposed for breaking a rule or law.

clue.text: Opening of honeypot? I'm not sure — tip from Pooh Bear

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
the tip of a word is its very end, here the first letter

blocks.note: the first letter
um is the hesitant noise of uncertainty
the first letter

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh dithers over whether to open the honey pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pooh Bear' reads as one name; Bear is the definition, the verb meaning carry. To hump is British slang for lugging something heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: To hump something is to carry it with effort, so it means to bear a load.

clue.text: Leaders of Newcastle usually taunt Sunderland fans

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Newcastle's bosses habitually mock the supporters of rival club Sunderland.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle and Sunderland are fierce north-east England football rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is an enthusiast, as in a football nut, so nuts are fans.

clue.text: Feature of numbers with natural base

blocks.note: nos is the abbreviation for numbers
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A mathematical property of numbers expressed in the natural base.
explanation.walkthrough: The maths setting makes 'feature' look like a property; it is a facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose is one of the facial features, along with eyes and mouth.

clue.text: Swimmers swim on vacation, including exercise by river

indicators.note: a word on vacation is vacated, emptied of its middle and left with its ends
including means taking something inside

blocks.note: the first and last letters
PE is physical education
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers swim and work out beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmers' looks like people in the water; it means the cells that swim to an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Sperm cells propel themselves with a tail, so they are cheekily called swimmers.

clue.text: Everybody loves a posh royal, one who's an old predator?

blocks.note: all means everybody
love is zero in tennis, the letter O, so loves are Os
taken as written
U means upper-class
R is the abbreviation for royal

explanation.surface: A toff-loving royal is unmasked as an old predator.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is old British slang for posh.
explanation.definitionFit: The allosaur was a large meat-eating dinosaur of the Jurassic, so an ancient hunter.
